newsitem.title: USA: Brooke's LeBow applauds settlement review.
newsitem.headline: Brooke's LeBow applauds settlement review.

text.p: The chairman of Brooke Group Ltd on Wednesday applauded proposals by former U.S. Surgeon General Everett Koop and former Food and Drug Administration Commissioner David Kessler to make a proposed tobacco settlement tougher on cigarette makers.

Brooke owns Liggett Group, which broke ranks with the other tobacco companies in March by reaching a separate settlement with U.S. state attorneys general. The company became the first to admit nicotine is addictive.

"Liggett applauds the findings in the Koop-Kessler report to broaden the provisions of the proposed settlement to permit the FDA to regulate nicotine, as Liggett has already agreed to similar provisions in its own settlements with the attorneys general of 25 states," Bennett LeBow, the chairman of Brooke, said in a statement.
"Liggett has acknowledged that nicotine is an addictive drug and has agreed to unfettered regulation by the FDA. Big Tobacco needs to do the same," he said.
LeBow said he would continue to work with the White House and members of Congress to ensure public health initiatives were attained and that Liggett's settlements were honored.
